text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police beat two opposition parliamentarians, journalists and several activists of the opposition Safina party during a tour of the Nyeri area.
- Opposition FORD Kenya party leaders rally around their Chairman Kijana Wamalwa and criticise the party vice-president condemnation of him.
- The Kenya Medical Association supports the government's ban of the alleged anti-AIDS drug Pearl Omega.
- The form one high school admissions deadline is extended because of famine.
- President Daniel arap Moi says civic education seminars are useless and the money used for them is enriching a few people.
- Armed gangsters raid a Nairobi estate, killing a resident and wounding three.
- Chief officers in Mombasa municipal council divide up a portion of a market destroyed by fire and set up permanent stalls.
- Nairobi's mayor warns residents to be wary of confidence tricksters allocating non-existent plots.
- More than 4,000 Roman Catholics attend a special healing crusade. ($1=55 Kenyan shillings)
